{"id": "d8187a1b-819a-4c95-9d3d-9c2f45cd613a", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_VOawIWlPsVWUbnShA20hGt", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"# Review Results\\\\n\\\\nEach completed investigation can be assessed by an automated reviewer against a\\\\nquality rubric. A review has an overall quality level (**helpful** or\\\\n**unhelpful**) and a set of per-dimension verdicts, each **pass**, **fail**, or\\\\n**not applicable**, with a one-sentence justification per dimension. A review\\\\nalso includes the stated root cause of the investigation.\\\\n\\\\n**The dimensions are configurable per agent space** \\\\u2014 a customer can edit the\\\\ngrading rubric (add, remove, or rename dimensions) via the grader\\'s `AGENTS.md`.\\\\nSo treat the dimension set as dynamic: report whatever dimensions each review\\\\nactually carries, and never assume a fixed list. The common default dimensions\\\\nare:\\\\n\\\\n- **Scope alignment** \\\\u2014 did the investigation address the actual alarm/problem?\\\\n- **Evidence grounding** \\\\u2014 are the conclusions backed by evidence?\\\\n- **Investigation completeness** \\\\u2014 can oncall act on the result?\\\\n- **Environment impact** \\\\u2014 do the deterministic signals support the verdict?\\\\n\\\\nA given agent space may have fewer, more, or differently named dimensions.\\\\n\\\\n**The rubric is editable.** The grading rubric lives in a **GRADER-scoped AGENTS.md**\\\\n(`agent_type` **GRADER**). If the user wants to change how investigations are graded \\\\u2014\\\\nadjust, add, drop, or rename dimensions, or change the HELPFUL/UNHELPFUL rule \\\\u2014 help them\\\\nedit that AGENTS.md. Express a priority as a prose rule, e.g. \\\\\"HELPFUL only if\\\\nscope_alignment passes\\\\\", rather than a numeric weight, since the Grader derives the verdict\\\\nfrom the per-dimension PASS/FAILs. To reset to the built-in defaults, delete the GRADER\\\\nAGENTS.md.\\\\n\\\\n## Viewing Results of All Reviews\\\\n\\\\n### USE-CASE-1: Summarize all reviews\\\\n\\\\n1. Call `list_grader_results`. Each entry is one completed review, carrying the\\\\n   reviewed investigation\\'s title (`investigationTitle`) and its `grade`. Use\\\\n   `createdAfter` / `createdBefore` for time-bounded requests (\\\\\"reviews from last\\\\n   week\\\\\"). Only reviewed investigations appear \\\\u2014 an unreviewed one has no entry.\\\\n2. Summarize the returned reviews: how many there are, the helpful vs. unhelpful\\\\n   split (`grade.quality_level`), and any recurring failing dimension across them.\\\\n3. If a `next_token` is returned and the user wants the full picture, page through\\\\n   with it before summarizing counts.\\\\n4. If no reviews come back, relay that none of their investigations have been\\\\n   reviewed yet (see the tool description) \\\\u2014 do not treat it as an error.\\\\n5. **Close** \\\\u2014 Offer to open a specific review or to save the summary.\\\\n\\\\n### USE-CASE-2: Compose a review-summary artifact\\\\n\\\\n1. Gather the data with `list_grader_results` (page through if needed).\\\\n2. Call `generate_artifact` with the collected review data and a clear instruction\\\\n   describing the deliverable \\\\u2014 e.g., a table of investigations with quality level\\\\n   and per-dimension verdicts, plus a chart of the helpful/unhelpful split. Pass\\\\n   the already-gathered data to `generate_artifact`; do not re-fetch it.\\\\n3. **Close** \\\\u2014 Point the user to the artifact and offer to drill into any review.\\\\n\\\\nFor a transient in-chat visual (not a saved report), prefer the\\\\n`render-inline-visual` skill instead of `generate_artifact`.\\\\n\\\\n## Viewing a Single Review\\\\n\\\\n### USE-CASE-3: One investigation\\'s review\\\\n\\\\n1. Identify the target investigation:\\\\n   - **Page context**: if `[now viewing: /investigation/<id>]` (or similar) is\\\\n     present, use that investigation.\\\\n   - **Conversation context**: if an investigation was just discussed, use it.\\\\n   - **Otherwise**: call `list_grader_results` and use `ask_user` to let the user\\\\n     pick which investigation\\'s review to open.\\\\n2. Call `get_grader_result` with the investigation\\'s task id.\\\\n3. Report the overall quality level and each dimension\\'s verdict with its\\\\n   justification. When a dimension failed, lead with the failing dimension and its\\\\n   reasoning.\\\\n4. **Close** \\\\u2014 Offer the full list of reviews or to open the investigation itself.\\\\n\\\\n### USE-CASE-4: Previous / earlier reviews of one investigation\\\\n\\\\nAn investigation is usually reviewed once, but a re-review produces additional\\\\nreviews. To retrieve them:\\\\n\\\\n1. Call `get_grader_result` with the investigation\\'s task id and\\\\n   `include_history: true`. See the tool\\'s own description for the exact response\\\\n   fields (current review plus the earlier ones and a total count).\\\\n2. If there are no earlier reviews, tell the user this investigation has only been\\\\n   reviewed once. Do not treat that as an error.\\\\n   **But** if the response also has `scan_window_exhausted: true`, the history may\\\\n   be incomplete (older reviews fell outside the scanned window) \\\\u2014 say the earlier\\\\n   reviews shown may not be the full history rather than asserting there was only\\\\n   one review.\\\\n3. When the user wants a comparison, contrast the current grade against the most\\\\n   recent previous one: call out quality-level changes (e.g. UNHELPFUL \\\\u2192 HELPFUL)\\\\n   and any dimension verdict that flipped, with the reasoning for each.\\\\n4. **Close** \\\\u2014 Offer to open the investigation or list all reviews.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Shared Guidance\\\\n\\\\n## Not-Yet-Reviewed Investigations\\\\n\\\\n- When `get_grader_result` reports no review for an investigation, tell the user it\\\\n  hasn\\'t been reviewed yet \\\\u2014 do not treat this as an error, and do not invent a grade.\\\\n- **But** when the tool\\'s response indicates its scan window was exhausted (see the\\\\n  tool description), do NOT say the investigation was never reviewed. Relay the tool\\'s\\\\n  own message \\\\u2014 a review may exist but is older \\\\u2014 and offer to narrow by time or open\\\\n  the investigation directly.\\\\n- When a listed review reports it couldn\\'t be loaded, skip it in your counts and, if\\\\n  relevant, note that one review couldn\\'t be loaded rather than failing the whole\\\\n  summary.\\\\n\\\\n## Tool Errors\\\\n\\\\nIf `list_grader_results` or `get_grader_result` returns an \\\\\"Unknown tool\\\\\" result:\\\\n\\\\n- The skill\\'s tools were dropped from this session. Call\\\\n  `skill_read(\\\\\"review-results\\\\\")` ONCE to reload them, then retry the original tool\\\\n  call ONCE.\\\\n- This is NOT an access/permission problem \\\\u2014 do not tell the user the feature is\\\\n  unavailable.\\\\n\\\\nOnly if a tool returns an explicit access-denied / authorization error (a\\\\npermissions message, not \\\\\"Unknown tool\\\\\"):\\\\n\\\\n- Do NOT retry the call.\\\\n- Explain the feature may not be enabled for their account.\\\\n\\\\n## Capability Boundaries\\\\n\\\\n- You CAN list reviews across investigations and open a single investigation\\'s\\\\n  review.\\\\n- You CAN summarize review results and compose an artifact from them.\\\\n- You CANNOT create, edit, re-run, or delete a review \\\\u2014 reviews are produced by a\\\\n  separate reviewer process, not on demand. You can only read the ones that exist.\\\\n- You CANNOT review an investigation on demand or promise to review one later.\\\\n\\\\n## Terminology\\\\n\\\\n- Refer to these as \\\\\"reviews\\\\\" and to the outcome as a \\\\\"quality level\\\\\" that is\\\\n  \\\\\"helpful\\\\\" or \\\\\"unhelpful\\\\\". Refer to each dimension in plain language, using\\\\n  whatever dimensions the review carries (the set is configurable per agent\\\\n  space \\\\u2014 do not assume a fixed four).\\\\n- Mirror the user\\'s vocabulary \\\\u2014 if they say \\\\\"grades\\\\\" or \\\\\"scores\\\\\", respond in kind.\\\\n- Never expose internal terms like \\\\\"grader\\\\\", \\\\\"taskId\\\\\", \\\\\"executionId\\\\\", \\\\\"agentType\\\\\",\\\\n  \\\\\"grader_output\\\\\", or \\\\\"journal record\\\\\".\"}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "8cfa0113-156e-4f02-a732-77598e8a8c36", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_mWel9TsEXmEzmnrrrnldsI", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"# Managing Skills from Chat\\\\n\\\\n## Skill Type Glossary\\\\n\\\\n| Type | Display Name | Description | Managed by |\\\\n|------|-------------|-------------|------------|\\\\n| **SYSTEM** | *(hidden)* | Built-in skills shipped with the agent (e.g. investigations, recommendations). Never visible to users. | Engineering team |\\\\n| **LEARNED** | Managed skills | Skills created by DevOps Agent. Editable and refreshed from Chat. | DevOps Agent / User (via Chat edits + refresh) |\\\\n| **USER** | Custom skills | Skills created and updated by the user through chat. Full CRUD operations supported. | User (via these tools) |\\\\n\\\\nSome managed skills can be refreshed through their dedicated tools.\\\\n\\\\n## Managed Skills Are Becoming Memories\\\\n\\\\nManaged (LEARNED) skills are migrating to memory stores: the same learned content, held as\\\\nmemories instead of a skill. The migration runs per agent space, so at any moment a given\\\\nkind may exist as a skill, as a memory store, or both during the transition.\\\\n\\\\n**When both exist for the same kind, the memory store is the home and the LEARNED skill is the\\\\nstale copy.** Read and edit the memory, not the skill, and tell the user where it now lives.\\\\n\\\\n1. When a request concerns learned understanding the DevOps Agent generates (the learned\\\\n   stores that the `manage-memories` skill\\'s glossary enumerates), check for a memory store of\\\\n   that name before reaching for `get_skill`.\\\\n2. If a memory store exists for it, load the `manage-memories` capability and work there,\\\\n   following its learned-store workflow.\\\\n3. If only the skill exists, this space has not migrated yet \\\\u2014 use the skill tools as below.\\\\n4. Do not \\\\\"fix\\\\\" a migrated skill by editing the leftover skill copy; that edit does not reach\\\\n   the agents now reading the memory.\\\\n\\\\n## Hard Rules\\\\n\\\\n- Create and delete apply only to custom (USER) skills \\\\u2014 managed (LEARNED) skills cannot be created or deleted from Chat.\\\\n- To edit a managed skill\\'s content, use `update_skill`. Do not silently substitute a custom skill that happens to share a name \\\\u2014 confirm you are editing the intended skill.\\\\n- Editing a managed (LEARNED) skill has refresh/durability considerations \\\\u2014 see \\\\\"Edit a Managed Skill\\\\\".\\\\n\\\\n## General\\\\n\\\\nWhen the user refers to a skill by name and you don\\'t have its knowledge_item_id, call `list_skills` to find it by name and confirm with the user before proceeding.\\\\n\\\\n## Operations\\\\n\\\\n### Create a Skill\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to create a skill:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Check for existing skills first** \\\\u2014 call `list_skills` and review the results. If an existing skill covers a similar domain or purpose, suggest updating it instead of creating a new one. For example, if the user asks to \\\\\"create a skill for RDS troubleshooting\\\\\" and there\\'s already an \\\\\"investigate-rds-issues\\\\\" skill, propose adding the new instructions to that skill. Only proceed with creation if no existing skill is a good fit, or the user explicitly wants a new one.\\\\n2. **Gather requirements** \\\\u2014 purpose, instructions, and whether the skill needs reference files\\\\n   - A skill only needs SKILL.md if the instructions fit in one document\\\\n   - Add reference files when the skill needs: runbook templates, API reference docs, configuration examples, troubleshooting decision trees, or service-specific guides that would bloat SKILL.md\\\\n   - Organize reference files by purpose: `references/` for documentation, `assets/` for templates and config files\\\\n   - Keep SKILL.md focused on the workflow and decision logic; put detailed reference material in separate files that the agent loads on demand\\\\n2. **Generate SKILL.md** with valid YAML frontmatter and markdown body\\\\n3. **Call `create_skill`** with title, content, and optionally resources\\\\n   - `create_skill(title=\\\\\"...\\\\\", content=\\\\\"...\\\\\")`\\\\n   - If the skill needs reference files: `create_skill(title=\\\\\"...\\\\\", content=\\\\\"...\\\\\", resources={\\\\\"references/guide.md\\\\\": \\\\\"# Guide content\\\\\", \\\\\"references/examples.md\\\\\": \\\\\"# Examples\\\\\"})`\\\\n4. **Show the user what was created** \\\\u2014 mention the skill name, description, and key steps. Do not show the ID.\\\\n5. **Ask the user to confirm** \\\\u2014 Use `ask_user` to confirm activation:\\\\n   ```\\\\n   ask_user(\\\\n     question=\\\\\"Would you like me to activate this skill?\\\\\",\\\\n     options=[\\\\n       {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Activate\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"Make this skill available for use\\\\\"},\\\\n       {\\\\\"label\\\\\": \\\\\"Keep inactive\\\\\", \\\\\"description\\\\\": \\\\\"Save the skill but don\\'t activate it yet\\\\\"}\\\\n     ]\\\\n   )\\\\n   ```\\\\n6. **On confirmation** \\\\u2014 call `activate_skill` with the knowledge_item_id to make it live\\\\n7. **The skill is now available** \\\\u2014 `create_skill` returns the skill content in its response, so you already have the instructions. No need to call `get_skill` separately. Close the flow in prose (e.g. \\\\\"Skill is now active.\\\\\"). Do not call `ask_user` again after activation \\\\u2014 no follow-up menus.\\\\n\\\\n### Update a Skill\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to edit or update a skill:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Read current content** \\\\u2014 use `get_skill` to get the current SKILL.md content\\\\n2. **Apply changes** \\\\u2014 modify the content as requested\\\\n3. **Call `update_skill`** with the knowledge_item_id and updated content\\\\n   - `update_skill(knowledge_item_id=\\\\\"...\\\\\", content=\\\\\"...\\\\\")`\\\\n   - To add a resource file: `update_skill(knowledge_item_id=\\\\\"...\\\\\", content=\\\\\"...\\\\\", resource_mutations=[{\\\\\"path\\\\\": \\\\\"references/new.md\\\\\", \\\\\"action\\\\\": \\\\\"ADD\\\\\", \\\\\"file_content\\\\\": \\\\\"# New content\\\\\"}])`\\\\n   - To edit a resource file: `update_skill(..., resource_mutations=[{\\\\\"path\\\\\": \\\\\"references/guide.md\\\\\", \\\\\"action\\\\\": \\\\\"EDIT\\\\\", \\\\\"file_content\\\\\": \\\\\"# Updated content\\\\\"}])`\\\\n   - To delete a resource file: `update_skill(..., resource_mutations=[{\\\\\"path\\\\\": \\\\\"references/old.md\\\\\", \\\\\"action\\\\\": \\\\\"DELETE\\\\\"}])`\\\\n   - Multiple mutations can be combined in a single call\\\\n\\\\n### Edit a Managed Skill (LEARNED)\\\\n\\\\nManaged skills hold learned content, so a direct edit follows the **same durability rule as a learned memory store**: it is **transient** \\\\u2014 the DevOps Agent\\'s next regeneration overwrites it. Confirm this kind has not already migrated to a memory store (see \\\\\"Managed Skills Are Becoming Memories\\\\\" above for that routing) before editing here, then apply the skill-specific mechanics below and tell the user a direct edit may not persist.\\\\n\\\\nSkill-specific mechanics for the direct edit:\\\\n1. **Confirm the target** \\\\u2014 read `skillKnowledgeItemId` from the page context.\\\\n2. **Make the edit** \\\\u2014 call `get_skill` for current content, then `update_skill`.\\\\n\\\\n### Delete a Skill\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to remove a skill:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Identify the skill** \\\\u2014 use `list_skills` if needed\\\\n2. **Confirm** \\\\u2014 always ask the user to confirm before deleting\\\\n3. **Call `delete_skill`** with the knowledge_item_id\\\\n4. **Report** \\\\u2014 confirm deletion\\\\n\\\\n### Read a Skill\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to see a skill\\'s content, explain what a skill does, or view its files:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Call `get_skill`** with the knowledge_item_id to get the SKILL.md content\\\\n2. **Explain** \\\\u2014 summarize the skill\\'s purpose, steps, and when it\\'s used\\\\n3. **If the skill has resource files** \\\\u2014 call `get_skill` with `return_manifest=true` to see all files, then use `path` to read specific resource files\\\\n\\\\n### List Skills\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to see their skills:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Call `list_skills`** \\\\u2014 returns agent space skills\\\\n2. **Present every skill individually** \\\\u2014 list each skill as a bullet: name \\\\u2014 description. Never group, merge, or deduplicate skills.\\\\n\\\\n### Enable or Disable a Skill\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to enable, disable, activate, or deactivate a skill:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Call `toggle_skill`** with the knowledge_item_id and `enabled=true` or `enabled=false`\\\\n2. **Report** \\\\u2014 confirm the new status. Disabled skills remain in the agent space but are not loaded by agents\\\\n\\\\n### Change Agent Type\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks to change which agent types can use a skill:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Call `update_skill_agent_type`** with the knowledge_item_id and the desired agent_types list \\\\u2014 see the tool\\'s `agent_types` parameter for the accepted values\\\\n2. **Report** \\\\u2014 confirm the new agent type targeting\\\\n\\\\n## SKILL.md Format\\\\n\\\\nCreate a valid SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter and markdown body:\\\\n\\\\n```markdown\\\\n---\\\\nname: my-skill-name\\\\ndescription: Brief description of what this skill does. Be specific about when\\\\n  the agent should use this skill (minimum 100 characters recommended).\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Skill Title\\\\n\\\\nInstructions for the agent when this skill is activated.\\\\n\\\\n## When to Use\\\\n- Condition 1\\\\n- Condition 2\\\\n\\\\n## Steps\\\\n1. Step one\\\\n2. Step two\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n### Frontmatter Rules\\\\n- `name`: Required. Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only (max 64 chars). Must not start or end with a hyphen. Example: `rds-throttling-investigation`\\\\n- `description`: Required. Brief explanation of when to use this skill (min 100 chars recommended, max 1024 chars).\\\\n\\\\n### Resource Files\\\\n\\\\nSkills can include reference files alongside SKILL.md. Reference files provide additional context the agent can load on demand. Use resource files when the skill needs supporting documentation, examples, API references, or other supplementary content.\\\\n\\\\n**Allowed file types:** `.md`, `.txt`, `.json`, `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.xml`, `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.html`, `.htm`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.svg`, `.webp`, `.pdf`\\\\n\\\\n**Restrictions:**\\\\n- No script files (`.sh`, `.py`, `.js`, `.ts`, `.rb`, `.pl`, `.ps1`, `.bat`, `.cmd`, `.exe`)\\\\n- No `scripts/` directory\\\\n- No files with shebang (`#!`) content\\\\n- Maximum 100 files, 6 MB total\\\\n\\\\n## Example\\\\n\\\\nUser: \\\\\"Create a skill that helps investigate Lambda cold start issues\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\n1. Generate SKILL.md:\\\\n```markdown\\\\n---\\\\nname: investigate-lambda-cold-starts\\\\ndescription: Investigate Lambda cold start latency issues by analyzing CloudWatch\\\\n  metrics, X-Ray traces, and function configuration. Use when users report slow\\\\n  Lambda response times or CloudWatch shows elevated Init Duration metrics.\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Investigating Lambda Cold Starts\\\\n\\\\n## When to Use\\\\n- User reports slow Lambda response times\\\\n- CloudWatch shows elevated Duration or Init Duration metrics\\\\n\\\\n## Steps\\\\n1. Every agent session sees this. |\\\\n| **CHAT** | On-demand | Chat agent only |\\\\n| **INCIDENT_RCA** | Investigation | Root cause analysis agent only |\\\\n| **INCIDENT_MITIGATION** | Mitigation | Mitigation agent only |\\\\n| **INCIDENT_TRIAGE** | Triage | Triage agent only |\\\\n| **RELEASE_READINESS_REVIEW** | Release Readiness | Release readiness review agent only |\\\\n| **GRADER** | Grader | Grader (investigation review) agent only |\\\\n\\\\nAny given agent session sees at most **2** AGENTS.md files: the GENERIC one (if it exists) plus the one for its specific agent type (if it exists).\\\\n\\\\n## Customizing an agent\\'s comments or output\\\\n\\\\nEach agent reads its agent-type AGENTS.md (plus GENERIC) on **every** run, so an AGENTS.md\\\\nis the way customers tune how a specific agent behaves \\\\u2014 including the **comments and output\\\\nit produces**. When creating or updating an AGENTS.md for this purpose, use the structure\\\\nbelow so the target agent actually honors the instructions.\\\\n\\\\n**Supported for the Release Readiness Review agent** \\\\u2014 the review agent honors only\\\\n*presentation* rules about the comments it writes:\\\\n- **Verbosity / length** \\\\u2014 e.g. terse one-line summaries vs. full detail.\\\\n- **Section include / exclude** \\\\u2014 which parts of a comment appear (impact, evidence,\\\\n  suggested fix, reproduction steps).\\\\n- **Tone / wording** \\\\u2014 voice and phrasing.\\\\n- **Terminology** \\\\u2014 how to name things in the comment text.\\\\n\\\\n**NOT supported \\\\u2014 do not promise these.** The review agent writes a comment for **every**\\\\nfinding it is given; it cannot filter, drop, or cap comments.
